name: com.contextpill/context-pill
title: Context Pill
description: Daily feed of AI releases, tools and techniques, each labeled with how it was checked.

tools.name: get_latest
tools.description: Returns today's checked items from the Context Pill feed (releases, tools, techniques), followed by attributed builder takes. The optional days parameter covers up to the last 14 days. Each checked claim has a verification status, a source trust score, evidence links, why it matters and an optional try-this step. The optional topic parameter filters by a word such as 'claude', 'codex' or 'open weights'. Fits questions about what's new in AI, recent models, tools, features, pricing or benchmarks. It covers what's new today or in recent days, not whether an older claim was checked or held up; search_claims covers that.

topic.description: Optional word to filter by, such as a vendor, product or model name. Leave empty for all checked claims and attributed takes in the days covered, up to the limit.

limit.description: Number of items to return, 1 to 30. Default 15.

days.description: Number of days to cover, 1 to 14, ending today (Los Angeles date). Default 1, today's drop only. Days with no drop are skipped.

tools.name: search_claims
tools.description: Searches every claim Context Pill has published (the ledger), including attributed builder takes. The query takes 1 to 3 key words, such as a product or model name: every word must appear somewhere in a result, so long queries often miss ('claude spreadsheet' works, a full sentence usually returns 0). For factual claims, returns status at publication, how it was checked, current state (pending, resolved, corrected, superseded (source changed its numbers after we checked) or closed-inconclusive), the 14-day re-check outcome and any correction. Corrected means a re-check found the claim wrong; the correction says what the source shows now when that could be read. Removed items keep only an id, date and reason, so they don't match. Zero matches says nothing about whether a claim is true. Fits questions about an AI launch, feature, price change, benchmark, leak or rumor, or whether something has shipped. Also fits being asked whether a claim was checked, was verified, held up or turned out to be wrong.

query.description: 1 to 3 key words, such as a product or model name, for example 'claude spreadsheet'. Case-insensitive. Common words such as 'is', 'the' or 'on' are ignored. Every other word must appear, so don't pass a full sentence.

limit.description: Number of claims to return, 1 to 30. Default 10.

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: Lists the sources Context Pill reads, with tier, trust score (posterior mean), its conservative lower bound (LB10) and the number of resolved tips. Every source starts at a neutral Beta(2,2) prior (trust 0.50) and moves when its claims are re-checked. The optional name parameter filters by source name. Fits questions about how far to trust the source behind an AI claim, including vendor claims.

name.description: Optional source name filter; may match more than one source. Leave empty to list all enabled sources.
